finding: Once legacyCloud=false is set through CLUSTERPROP, a plain SPLITSHARD of shard1 fails every time. The Overseer sends the sub-shard leader core-admin CREATE without a coreNodeName, and CoreAdminHandler rejects it ('non legacy mode coreNodeName missing'), so the split aborts with 'SPLITSHARD failed to create subshard leaders'.
same_root_cause: Yes. In the buggy OverseerCollectionProcessor.splitShard (OverseerCollectionProcessor.java:1335-1347) the Overseer queues the createshard message and then sends a bare CoreAdmin CREATE (name/collection/shard only) through sendShardRequest. It never registers a replica in cluster state and never sets a coreNodeName. The sub-shard replica CREATE at :1468-1486 has the same gap. The CREATE lands in CoreAdminHandler.java:557-560 (ZkController present, !isLegacy, coreNodeName==null) and throws. The fix hunks @@ -1332 and @@ -1463 remove exactly these bare CREATE requests: they wait for the new slice (waitForNewShard) and then go through addReplica, which registers the replica and passes its coreNodeName. validate-1.log line 2650 shows the rejected CREATE for collection1_shard1_0_replica1 coming from the Overseer's splitshard.
realistic: Yes. The trigger is ordinary: a mini cluster (ShardSplitTest's setup), an admin setting the supported cluster property legacyCloud=false through the Collections API, and a normal SPLITSHARD request. There is no reflection, no mocking and no fault injection. The fix's own test change in ShardSplitTest sets the same property in the same way.
fixed_version: On the buggy tree plus the fix's production changes, the same test passed in 4 of 4 runs (BUILD SUCCESSFUL), and 'coreNodeName missing' appears in none of the fixed logs. On the buggy tree it reproduced on the first run (the check's exception at CoreAdminHandler.java:560).
reason: The agent's test hits the exact defect SOLR-6101 fixes: with legacyCloud=false, SPLITSHARD creates sub-shard cores through a core-admin CREATE that has no coreNodeName, because the Overseer has not registered the replica first. The trigger is realistic, and the consequence matches the JIRA (shard splitting does not work with legacyCloud=false). The fixed version no longer fails.
